title: Count Covered Buildings
summary: Given a positive integer n for an n x n city and a 2D grid of buildings, count how many buildings are covered by at least one building in all four cardinal directions.
statement: Given a positive integer n for an n x n city and a 2D grid of buildings, count how many buildings are covered by at least one building in all four cardinal directions.
constraints: Buildings are unique integer coordinates within an n by n city; there may be up to 100,000.
A building is covered only when another exists left and right in its row and above and below in its column.
Return the number of covered buildings.
hints: Only the extreme occupied coordinates in each row and column matter for four-direction coverage.
Record minimum and maximum y per row and x per column.
For each building, count it when its y lies strictly between its row extremes and x strictly between its column extremes.
Strict interior position is equivalent to having at least one occupied coordinate on each required side.
editorial: Strict interior position is equivalent to having at least one occupied coordinate on each required side.

tests.explanation: Only the center building has neighbors on both row sides and both column sides.
Every building is extreme in its row or column, so none is covered.
